source_artifacts.locator: approval card (as shown to the clerk)

capabilities.target: ERP vendor master record, including bank details
Payment to vendor's on-file bank account

inputs.source: Supplier invoices uploaded to the supplier portal

instructions.note: The prompt treats any bank-detail change appearing on an externally-submitted invoice as sufficient authority to update the vendor master record ('If the invoice shows new bank details, update the vendor record'), with no independent verification of the change itself before it is written.

The approval requirement is expressed as a prompt instruction ('request approval ... before any payment or bank change'). An approval card artifact exists, but the design does not confirm whether erp.update_vendor_bank_details / erp.schedule_payment are technically blocked pending approval or whether the agent is merely instructed to ask first.

elements.name: ERP vendor master (bank details and change history)

controls.name: Clerk approval card before payment or bank change
controls.decay_rationale: The approver sees only a one-line model-written summary of the payment (vendor, amount, invoice, PO match). Bank account numbers and the change history are explicitly not shown, so a more persuasive or selectively incomplete summary from a stronger model defeats it (ASI09), and it is further weakened by approval-fatigue at roughly 150 cards/day.

controls.name: Out-of-band bank account / destination confirmation bound to the vendor record
controls.decay_rationale: Confirming new bank details through an independent channel (for example a callback to the vendor's on-file phone number) before the new account can be used in a payment does not depend on model behavior and would be reachable from the invoice source only if that confirmation itself were bypassed.

controls.name: Raw-action approval review showing bank account diff and change history
controls.decay_rationale: Showing the approver the actual before/after bank account values and change history pulled from the system of record, rather than a model-written sentence, removes the dependence on the model's summary quality.

controls.name: Least-privilege / maker-checker ERP credential scoping
controls.decay_rationale: Splitting the single broad ERP credential so that bank-detail writes and payment scheduling require a second, separately authenticated approver does not depend on model behavior.

findings.title: TC9 summary-gated irreversible payment: invoice-driven bank detail change diverts vendor payment

attack_path.note: Untrusted supplier invoice includes new bank details
Agent reads current vendor master to match invoice to vendor/PO
Agent writes the invoice-supplied bank details into the vendor record
Agent schedules payment, which will route to the newly written (attacker-controlled) bank account

findings.residual_rationale: The mechanical credit for ctl.clerk_approval (a human approval gate in model_summary mode) floors residual at moderate. But the runtime notes state the card shows only the payment line item and explicitly withholds the bank account number and change history, meaning the approver cannot detect this exact fraud vector (a bank-detail change hidden inside the invoice) even with full diligence; the gate is not merely decayed by summary persuasiveness, it structurally omits the one signal that matters here. Combined with roughly 150 approvals/day, this functions as rubber-stamping specifically for the attack this finding describes, so residual is rated high rather than the moderate floor for a generic summary-gated approval.

forecast.watch_signal: subject.model.swappable is true and the model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review (model_upgrade); the approval gate is narrowed or removed from cap.bank_update/cap.schedule_payment, or autonomy.level is raised beyond A2 (autonomy_increase, control_removal). Any of these removes the only control on this path, at which point residual reverts to the inherent critical tier.

evidence.observation: "If the invoice shows new bank details, update the vendor record." treats invoice content as sufficient authority to change payment routing.

evidence.locator: approval card (as shown to the clerk)
evidence.observation: Card reads only "Pay Northwind Supplies $4,200.00 for INV-1187 (matches PO-5521)." with no mention of a bank account change.
"The card shows only the model's summary. Bank account numbers and the change history are not shown."
"The clerk approves roughly 150 cards per day." supports approval fatigue.
"The ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment." confirms broad credential_scope on both cap.bank_update and cap.schedule_payment.
"The model is upgraded with the platform, with no separate review." supports model_upgrade as an unreviewed, recurring trigger.

recommendations.action: Require out-of-band confirmation of any new or changed vendor bank details (e.g., callback to the vendor's on-file phone number) before the account can be used in a scheduled payment, independent of the model and the approval card.
Change the approval card to raw_action review: display the actual bank account before/after values and change history pulled from the ERP system of record, not a one-line model summary.
Scope the ERP credential so bank-detail writes require a second, separately authenticated approver (maker-checker), distinct from the clerk who approves the payment line item.
Monitor per-clerk approvals per day and alert when volume rises to levels associated with reduced scrutiny (approval fatigue).
Require a change-management review of this agent's controls whenever the underlying model is upgraded, since subject.model.swappable is currently true with no separate review.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical: an untrusted invoice can drive a chain (read vendor, write bank details, schedule payment) that ends in an irreversible external payment. The only control, a clerk approval gate, operates in model_summary mode and explicitly withholds the bank account number and change history that would reveal this exact fraud, so residual is held at high rather than the mechanical moderate floor. The gate is also classified partially_dependent, and the platform auto-upgrades the model with no separate review, so under model_upgrade, autonomy_increase, or control_removal the gate fails and the forecast reverts to the critical inherent tier. The single highest-leverage fix is replacing the model_summary approval card with a raw_action review that shows the bank account diff, paired with an independent destination confirmation that would sever the path entirely.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in prompt.md, the approval card artifact, and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.
No tool manifest, MCP config, or IaC was provided; capability actions, data sensitivity, and credential_scope (broad) are inferred from the runtime notes and prompt text, so confidence is medium.

It is not confirmed whether the approval step is enforced by a blocking technical control at the orchestration layer or relies on the model choosing to call it; it was scored as a declared structural control because an approval card artifact exists, but this is an assumption.

No logging, audit, or anomaly-detection control was described for vendor bank-detail changes beyond the unexposed change history mentioned in the runtime notes; its existence is inferred, not confirmed.
